newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk refinery unions threaten strike on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk refinery unions threaten strike on Friday.

text.p: The four trade unions at Poland's Gdansk refinery Rafineria Gdanska SA will stage a warning strike of at least one hour on Friday, the head of the Solidarity trade union at the refinery said on Wednesday.

Andrzej Cenacewicz told Reuters that the action would be in solidarity with the workers of the ailing Gdansk Shipyard, 3,800 of whom face lay-offs, and in protest against a failure to issue free shares in the refinery.

"We've agreed on strike action for this coming Friday and it's being discussed whether to stop work for an hour, two or more," Cenacewicz said, adding that the issue would continue until a decision came granting the employees the shares.
The Gdansk refinery's largest shareholder is state-owned oil holding Nafta Polska SA, which has 75 percent of shares.
The unions are demanding 15 percent of shares they say are due them shortly after a new law on the privatisation of state firms goes into effect on April 8.
The government has said that more details on the firm's privatisation must be decided on before the shares are granted.

The unions have written to the cabinet and parliament saying they are concerned with the refinery's worsening financial results, for which they blame the policies of the current government led by ex-communists.

"We note the worsening financial results of the firm even though 1996 was a record year of crude oil processing and the sale of products. The cause of this we see in the poor policies of the government," the letter said.
Preliminary figures show the Gdansk refinery's 1996 net profit falling 35 percent from 1995's 125 million zlotys.
Sales grew 12 percent last year to 3.2 billion zlotys.
Analysts have said the falling profitability of Polish refineries has been caused by the government keeping official limits on fuel prices until last month, despite high world crude prices.
